verdicts.rationale: Both are diagnostic tests for heteroskedasticity, offering alternative approaches to checking variance assumptions in regression models.
Robust standard errors correct the unreliability of standard standard errors caused by heteroskedasticity.
You use diagnostic tests like the Breusch-Pagan test to determine if you need to apply robust standard errors.
Robust standard errors are designed to provide valid inference precisely when the assumption of homoskedasticity fails.
Detecting heteroskedasticity using tests like the White test motivates the subsequent use of robust standard errors.
Detecting heteroskedasticity with the Breusch-Pagan test can guide your decision to use weighted least squares to correct it.
Identifying heteroskedasticity through the Goldfeld-Quandt test helps inform when to apply weighted least squares.
The Breusch-Pagan test is specifically designed to test for the presence of heteroskedasticity.
